title: The sheaf of lattices is a separated étale scheme
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ and its topological valuation ring $A=\cO_E$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Use universes containing the schemes, coefficient rings and the set of lattices below [def-weil-size-convention]. On the small pro-étale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], $E_X$ and $A_X$ are the pullbacks of the condensed topological rings $E$ and $A$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]; modules are module objects [sk-def-sfb-module-objects]. Here lisse means pro-étale locally free of finite rank, and a lattice is an embedded lisse $A_X$-module whose localization at $\ell$ is the ambient rational module. Constant sheaf means sheafification of the constant presheaf [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. A scheme is qcqs if its underlying space is quasi-compact and its diagonal is quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Separated and étale have the meanings of [def-weil-proper-morphism] and [def-weil-etale-morphism].

Let $X$ be a qcqs scheme and $L$ a lisse $E_X$-module of constant rank $r$. Let $\mathcal{L}\mathit{at}$
be the sheaf on $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$ with $\mathcal{L}\mathit{at}(U)$ the set of lisse
$\cO_{E,U}$-submodules $M\subseteq L|_U$ with $M[1/\ell]=L|_U$.

1. If $L|_V\cong E_V^r$ on $V$, then $\mathcal{L}\mathit{at}|_V$ is the constant sheaf on the discrete set
   $\GL_r(E)/\GL_r(\cO_E)$ of $\cO_E$-lattices in $E^r$.
2. $\mathcal{L}\mathit{at}$ is represented by a separated étale $X$-scheme $\mathrm{Lat}(L)\to X$, which is
   surjective.
3. There is a universal lattice $M^{\mathrm{univ}}\subseteq q^*L$ on $\mathrm{Lat}(L)$,
   $q\colon\mathrm{Lat}(L)\to X$.

proof.text: Identify the reconstructed internal coefficient sheaves with continuous coefficient sheaves using [lem-sfb-continuous-ring-universe-realization]. Naturality follows from the adjoint comparison on profinite tests. Transport lattice pairs along this commuting coefficient square using the construction of [lem-weil-pbc-integral-lattice-coefficient-transport], recording the image of each pure tensor 1 tensor m. The sheafification unit and its naturality show that embedded images are preserved. The image criterion in [lem-weil-pbc-lattice-pair-image-classification] then transports the exact lattice-class presentation, including restriction maps. Transport free charts through the rational coefficient isomorphism, and apply [lem-weil-pbc-lattice-sheaf-locally-constant] to obtain the sheaf and the required constant-coset isomorphisms.

The image presentation makes every section a class of subobjects of a fixed module. Use [lem-weil-pbc-lisse-lattice-presentation-transport] to shrink the presentation and transport slice trivializations to the small pro-etale site. Refine the given CoversTop family to a precoverage family. Apply [lem-sfb-local-system-affine-descent-presentation] to obtain the affine weakly etale, flat, surjective, quasi-compact fpqc chart p:V to X and its representing coproduct with scheme descent datum.

Apply [lem-sfb-coproduct-fpqc-effectivity] to this affine chart and datum. Its quasi-affine quasi-compact-open calculation verifies effectivity even when $S$ is infinite. Obtain $q:Y\to X$ and $\eta:Y\times_XV\simeq T$ inducing that datum.

Use [lem-sfb-coproduct-model-represents-sheaf] with the local representing bijections and $\eta$. It gives natural bijections $F(U)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}_X(U,Y)$ and makes $q$ separated and étale. The standard lattice supplies a label of $S$ for every $r\geq0$, so $q$ is surjective. Set $\mathrm{Lat}(L)=Y$, proving (2).

The natural representing bijections, composed with the size-change bijections and the canonical universe lift, give the stated presheaf isomorphism rho. Surjectivity of the lattice-class presentation at the representing object supplies a lattice pair mapping to the inverse image of the identity. The inverse identities of these bijections prove precisely the universal-lattice equation in (3).

For $r=0$, $S$ is a singleton and the only lattice is zero, so the representing sheaf is terminal and $Y=X$. For empty $X$ use the empty covering and empty representing scheme. The four cited lemmas include these cases.

proof_origin.place: (1)-(3); explicit coefficient-square and lattice-image transport, followed by the prescribed affine coproduct fpqc descent route; C3 Lean assembly
